functions.name: lgraph_api::base64::Encode
functions.signature: inline std::string lgraph_api::base64::Encode(const char* p, size_t s)
functions.description: Encode raw bytes [p, p+s) into a Base64-encoded ASCII string. Intended for simple BLOB encoding.
requirements: If s > 0, p must point to at least s readable bytes; if s == 0, p may be null.
Returns a string padded with '=' per Base64 rules.

functions.name: lgraph_api::base64::TryDecode
functions.signature: inline bool lgraph_api::base64::TryDecode(const char* p, size_t s, std::string& ret)
functions.description: Attempt to decode a Base64-encoded buffer p of length s into ret. Returns true on success, false on invalid input.
requirements: If s > 0, p must point to at least s readable bytes; if s == 0, p may be null.
s must be a multiple of 4; otherwise returns false (explicit).
All characters must be valid Base64 (A–Z, a–z, 0–9, '+', '/') or '=' padding; otherwise returns false (explicit).
On success, ret is resized to decoded size; on failure, ret contents are unspecified beyond attempted resize.

_patterns = [
    b"",  # empty
    b"A",  # single ascii
    b"\x00",  # single NUL
    b"\xff",  # single 0xFF
    b"ABC",  # ascii 3
    b"abcd",  # ascii 4
    b"\x00\x01\x02",  # low bytes
    bytes(range(256)),  # 0..255 sequence
    bytes(range(255, -1, -1)),  # 255..0 reverse
    b"\x00\xff" * 64,  # alternating extremes
    b"\x7f\x80" * 64,   # around signed boundary
    b"\x00" * 512,  # zeros
    b"\xff" * 512,  # all ones
    b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
]

# Common multiples of 3 and neighbors to stress Base64 padding behavior
_b64_boundary_lengths = [
    0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 30, 33, 60, 63, 66, 93, 120
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _repeat_to_len(data: bytes, n: int) -> bytes:
    if not data:
        return b"" if n == 0 else b"\x00" * n
    full, rem = divmod(n, len(data))
    return data * full + data[:rem]


def _choose_length(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias to interesting boundaries (multiples of 3 for Base64, and +/-1 around them)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base = rng.choice(_b64_boundary_lengths)
        delta = rng.choice([-2, -1, 0, 1, 2])
        n = max(0, base + delta)
    else:
        n = rng.randint(0, min(_MAX_SIZE, 2048))
    # Occasionally pick from predefined interesting lengths
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        n = rng.choice(_def_interesting_lengths)
    return min(n, _MAX_SIZE)


def _compose_buffer(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix several construction strategies
    choice = rng.random()
    if n == 0:
        return b""
    if choice < 0.15:
        # Pure random
        return _rand_bytes(rng, n)
    elif choice < 0.30:
        # Repeat a short random chunk
        chunk_len = rng.randint(1, min(64, max(1, n)))
        chunk = _rand_bytes(rng, chunk_len)
        return _repeat_to_len(chunk, n)
    elif choice < 0.45:
        # Pick a predefined pattern and trim/extend
        pat = rng.choice(_patterns)
        return _repeat_to_len(pat, n)
    elif choice < 0.60:
        # Gradient sequence 0..255 cycling starting at a random offset
        start = rng.randrange(256)
        seq = bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(min(256, n)))
        return _repeat_to_len(seq, n)
    elif choice < 0.75:
        # Blocks of specific bytes
        b1, b2 = rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256)
        block1 = bytes([b1]) * rng.randint(1, max(1, n // 2))
        block2 = bytes([b2]) * (n - len(block1))
        return block1 + block2
    else:
        # Structured mix: header + body + tail with different distributions
        header_len = min(n, rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 16]))
        tail_len = min(max(0, n - header_len), rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8]))
        body_len = max(0, n - header_len - tail_len)
        header = bytes(range(header_len))
        body = _rand_bytes(rng, body_len)
        tail = bytes(range(255, 255 - tail_len, -1)) if tail_len > 0 else b""
        return header + body + tail


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    n = _choose_length(rng)
    data = _compose_buffer(rng, n)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > _MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:_MAX_SIZE]
    return data

import random
import base64
from typing import List

# We generate valid Base64-encoded ASCII buffers (no whitespace),
# length is a multiple of 4, may include padding '='. Also sometimes empty.
# We try to cover interesting cases: different lengths, different padding (0/1/2 '=')
# and content patterns (all bytes, textual ASCII, long runs, repeating blocks).

_ASCII_TEXT = (
    b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. "
    b"Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. "
)

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _repeat_pattern(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a small pattern and repeat it up to max_len
    patterns = [
        b"\x00",
        b"\xff",
        b"\x00\xff",
        b"ABC",
        b"\x13\x37",
        b"\x00ABC\xff",
    ]
    p = rng.choice(patterns)
    reps = max(1, min(max_len // max(1, len(p)), rng.randint(1, max_len)))
    data = (p * reps)[:max_len]
    # Occasionally add a tail of random few bytes
    if len(data) < max_len and rng.random() < 0.4:
        tail = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, max_len - len(data)))
        data += tail
    return data

def _mix_sources(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Blend ASCII text chunks with random bytes
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len:
        choice = rng.random()
        remaining = target_len - len(out)
        if choice < 0.5:
            # ASCII slice
            start = rng.randint(0, max(0, len(_ASCII_TEXT) - 1)) if _ASCII_TEXT else 0
            slen = rng.randint(1, max(1, min(64, remaining)))
            out += _ASCII_TEXT[start:start + slen]
        elif choice < 0.8:
            # random bytes
            out += _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, min(64, remaining)))
        else:
            # small numeric ASCII chunk
            num = str(rng.getrandbits(64)).encode()
            out += num[:remaining]
    return bytes(out[:target_len])

def _choose_raw_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Pick a strategy and length for the raw bytes that will be Base64-encoded
    # Keep encoded output <= 4096 bytes. Base64 expands ~4/3, plus padding.
    max_raw = 3000  # safe upper bound (3000 -> 4000 encoded)
    strategy = rng.choices(
        population=["empty", "small_rand", "small_ascii", "pattern", "mixed", "boundary"],
        weights=[1, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if strategy == "empty":
        return b""
    if strategy == "small_rand":
        n = rng.randint(1, 128)
        return _rand_bytes(rng, n)
    if strategy == "small_ascii":
        n = rng.randint(1, 256)
        return (_ASCII_TEXT * ((n // len(_ASCII_TEXT)) + 1))[:n]
    if strategy == "pattern":
        n = rng.randint(1, 2048)
        return _repeat_pattern(rng, n)
    if strategy == "mixed":
        n = rng.randint(1, 2048)
        return _mix_sources(rng, n)
    # boundary: craft lengths that yield specific padding behaviors after Base64
    kind = rng.choice([0, 1, 2])
    # Base64 padding rules:
    # len%3==0 -> no '='; len%3==1 -> '=='; len%3==2 -> '='
    base = rng.randint(1, max_raw - 3)
    base -= base % 3
    if kind == 0:
        length = base  # no padding
    elif kind == 1:
        length = base + 1  # '=='
    else:
        length = base + 2  # '='
    length = max(1, min(max_raw, length))
    return _mix_sources(rng, length)

def _maybe_make_multiple_of_4_ascii(rng: random.Random, b64_bytes: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Our encoding already yields multiple of 4. But to exercise harness branches,
    # occasionally return substrings that are still valid Base64 and multiple of 4
    # (e.g., cut at 4-char boundary). Do this rarely to keep inputs valid.
    if not b64_bytes:
        return b64_bytes
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        # choose a multiple-of-4 cut
        max_quads = len(b64_bytes) // 4
        if max_quads > 0:
            quads = rng.randint(0, max_quads)  # allow 0 to produce empty
            return b64_bytes[: quads * 4]
    return b64_bytes

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a raw payload and encode to Base64 without newlines
    raw = _choose_raw_payload(rng)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(raw)

    # Optionally trim to a multiple-of-4 boundary (still valid)
    b64 = _maybe_make_multiple_of_4_ascii(rng, b64)

    # Sometimes return empty to exercise s==0 path
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        return b""

    # Ensure length <= 4096
    if len(b64) > 4096:
        # Trim to nearest multiple of 4 while preserving validity
        b64 = b64[: (4096 // 4) * 4]

    return b64
